# Part 1: Measurement and mathematical foundations

```{=latex}
\markright{Engineering notation and SI prefixes}
```

## Engineering notation and SI prefixes {.unnumbered}

For a nonzero value, engineering notation uses $a\times10^{3n}$ with $1\leq |a|<1000$. The exponent is a multiple of three, so the value converts directly to an SI prefix. Write zero as $0$.

| Value | Engineering form | Prefix form |
|:--|:--|:--|
| $0.000\,047\ \mathrm{A}$ | $47\times10^{-6}\ \mathrm{A}$ | $47\ \mu\mathrm{A}$ |
| $0.0047\ \mathrm{A}$ | $4.7\times10^{-3}\ \mathrm{A}$ | $4.7\ \mathrm{mA}$ |
| $4700\ \Omega$ | $4.7\times10^3\ \Omega$ | $4.7\ \mathrm{k}\Omega$ |
| $2\,200\,000\ \mathrm{Hz}$ | $2.2\times10^6\ \mathrm{Hz}$ | $2.2\ \mathrm{MHz}$ |

| Exponent | Prefix | Symbol |
|:--:|:--|:--:|
| $10^9$ | giga | $\mathrm{G}$ |
| $10^6$ | mega | $\mathrm{M}$ |
| $10^3$ | kilo | $\mathrm{k}$ |
| $10^0$ | base unit | - |
| $10^{-3}$ | milli | $\mathrm{m}$ |
| $10^{-6}$ | micro | $\mu$ |
| $10^{-9}$ | nano | $\mathrm{n}$ |
| $10^{-12}$ | pico | $\mathrm{p}$ |

Choose the exponent that keeps the coefficient from $1$ up to, but not including, $1000$. For example, $999\ \Omega$ stays $999\ \Omega$, while $1000\ \Omega$ becomes $1\ \mathrm{k}\Omega$.

## H01 Safety and lab practice

A safe electronics workflow begins with a prediction, a current-limited source, a power-off inspection, correct meter setup, and a deliberate decision to energize. Protection belongs near the source so a conductor fault does not leave an unprotected energized path.

::: {.content-visible when-format="html"}
![A protected 9 V classroom circuit with a source, fuse, switch, resistor, and LED in one series path.](../schematics/H01_Safety_Lab_Practice_Schematic.svg){width=100%}
:::

::: {.content-visible when-format="pdf"}
![A protected 9 V classroom circuit with a source, fuse, switch, resistor, and LED in one series path.](../schematics/H01_Safety_Lab_Practice_Schematic.pdf){width=100%}
:::

| Check | Evidence |
|:--|:--|
| source | voltage and current limit |
| protection | fuse rating and location |
| control | switch starts open |
| load | polarity, value, and power rating |
| measurement | correct jack, function, range, and placement |

**Worked GUESS check:** With $V_S=9.0\ \mathrm{V}$, $V_F=2.0\ \mathrm{V}$, and $R=330\ \Omega$, $I=(9.0-2.0)/330=21\ \mathrm{mA}$. Casio entry: `( 9.0 - 2.0 ) ÷ 330 =`.

**Warning:** Disconnect immediately for heat, smell, smoke, unstable connections, or uncertainty. Never use an ohmmeter on an energized circuit.

**Application and links:** Protected indicators, bicycle lights, and low-voltage controls. [H01 notes](https://andrewandrade.ca/tech-edu-resources/tej3-4/electronics-library/modules/h01-safety-lab-practice.html), worksheet, simulation guide, lab, and slides are linked from the module page.

## H02 Charge, current, voltage, and energy

Charge is an amount of electric charge. Current is the rate of charge flow. Voltage is energy transferred per unit charge. Energy records the total work transferred over time.

| Quantity | Relationship | Unit |
|:--|:--|:--|
| charge | $Q=It$ | coulomb, $\mathrm{C}$ |
| current | $I=Q/t$ | ampere, $\mathrm{A}$ |
| voltage | $V=W/Q$ | volt, $\mathrm{V}$ |
| energy | $E=Pt$ | joule, $\mathrm{J}$ |

**When it applies:** Use these definitions to connect current and time, or power and operating time. Keep seconds with watts for joules. Use hours with watts for watt-hours.

**Worked GUESS example:** A $0.25\ \mathrm{A}$ device runs for $120\ \mathrm{s}$. $Q=It=(0.25)(120)=30\ \mathrm{C}$. Casio entry: `0.25 × 120 =`.

**Common mistake:** Ampere-hours describe charge capacity, not energy, unless voltage is also considered.

**Application and links:** Battery capacity, USB loads, and vehicle accessories. [Course notes](https://andrewandrade.ca/tech-edu-resources/tej3-4/02-basic-electronics/01-charge-voltage-current.html).

\newpage\markright{H03 AC versus DC}

## H03 AC versus DC

Direct current keeps one reference polarity. Alternating current changes direction and usually changes magnitude with time. A waveform must include amplitude, period, frequency, and reference polarity.

| Quantity | Relationship | Unit |
|:--|:--|:--|
| period and frequency | $f=1/T$ | hertz, $\mathrm{Hz}$ |
| sine-wave RMS | $V_{\mathrm{RMS}}=V_P/\sqrt{2}$ | volt, $\mathrm{V}$ |
| peak-to-peak | $V_{PP}=2V_P$ | volt, $\mathrm{V}$ |

**Worked GUESS example:** For $T=20.0\ \mathrm{ms}$, $f=1/(20.0\times10^{-3})=50.0\ \mathrm{Hz}$. Casio entry: `1 ÷ ( 20 EXP (-) 3 ) =`.

**Warning:** Classroom breadboards and handheld meters must not connect directly to mains. Use approved isolated low-voltage sources.

**Application and links:** Batteries supply DC. Wall adapters often rectify AC into DC. Alternators and audio signals produce changing waveforms. See [All About Circuits](https://www.allaboutcircuits.com/textbook/alternating-current/).

\newpage\markright{H04 Schematic symbols and circuit anatomy}

## H04 Schematic symbols and circuit anatomy

A schematic shows electrical relationships rather than physical layout. Nodes joined by an uninterrupted conductor share the same ideal voltage. A crossing without a junction dot does not automatically mean a connection.

| Block | Function |
|:--|:--|
| source | supplies electrical energy |
| protection | opens or limits an abnormal condition |
| control | changes the intended operating state |
| load | converts electrical energy |
| conductor | completes the intended path |

**When it applies:** Draw a proper schematic before simulation or physical construction. Label component references and values. Keep a separate wiring or breadboard layout when physical placement matters.

**Worked check:** Trace from the source through protection, control, load, and back to the source. If any intended series connection is open, current is zero.

**Common mistake:** A lamp symbol and LED arrows describe different devices. Use a proper LED symbol with a separate current-limiting resistor.

**Application and links:** Service manuals, PCB design, simulation, and troubleshooting. Related H01 downloads are on the [electronics library](https://andrewandrade.ca/tech-edu-resources/tej3-4/electronics-library/).

## H05 Multimeter fundamentals

The meter connection depends on the measured quantity. A voltmeter compares two nodes. An ammeter becomes part of the current path. An ohmmeter supplies its own test signal and therefore requires an isolated, de-energized circuit.

| Measurement | Placement | State |
|:--|:--|:--|
| voltage | parallel | energized if approved |
| current | series | energized after setup check |
| resistance or continuity | across isolated part | power off and discharged |

**Expected-reading example:** In an open series circuit, current is $0\ \mathrm{A}$. The open switch can have the full source voltage across it while intact components have zero current-produced drop.

**Warning:** Never place a current-configured meter directly across a source. Return the red lead from the current jack after the reading.

**Application and links:** Bench diagnosis, continuity checks, supply verification, and component screening. Use the H01 lab and [measurement notes](https://andrewandrade.ca/tech-edu-resources/tej3-4/electronics-library/modules/h01-safety-lab-practice.html).

\newpage\markright{H06 Resistance and resistor identification}

## H06 Resistance and resistor identification

Resistance relates voltage to current and converts electrical energy into heat. A resistor selection needs resistance, tolerance, power rating, and a suitable package.

| Relationship | Use |
|:--|:--|
| $R=V/I$ | calculate required resistance |
| $P=I^2R$ | check resistor heating |
| $G=1/R$ | convert to conductance |

**Worked GUESS example:** A resistor has $5.0\ \mathrm{V}$ across it and carries $10.0\ \mathrm{mA}$. $R=5.0/(10.0\times10^{-3})=500\ \Omega$. Casio entry: `5.0 ÷ ( 10.0 EXP (-) 3 ) =`.

**Common mistake:** The colour code gives nominal value and tolerance. It does not guarantee the resistor can dissipate the calculated power.

**Application and links:** Current limiting, bias networks, dividers, timing networks, and sensor interfaces. See the [component index](https://andrewandrade.ca/tech-edu-resources/tej3-4/electronics-library/components/).
